**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/21 (Sun) 08:09  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant confirmed the renaming of the `NewVHDName` parameter to `NewVMName` in the provided script.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] The assistant provided an updated PowerShell script that includes parameters for `$VMName`, `$VMPath`, `$NewVMName`, `$MemoryStartupBytes`, and `$CPUCount`.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explained that the script will rename the old VM configuration to "${VMName}_Gen1" and create a new VM configuration named "${VMName}_Gen2".  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned that if the `-MemoryStartupBytes` and `-CPUCount` parameters are omitted, the VM will default to 4 GB of memory and 4 CPU cores.  
[USER] The user inquired whether the script would copy over all network adapters from the old VM configuration to the new one, emphasizing the need for them to come over 100% as-is.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant clarified that the updated script would only copy over the first network adapter from the old VM configuration to the new one.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] The assistant provided an updated script that includes a `foreach` loop to copy over all network adapters from the old VM configuration to the new one.  
[USER] The user asked about re-attaching any vhdx files present in the old VM configuration to the new one, specifically omitting the converted vhdx being created in the script.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant agreed to modify the script to re-attach any additional virtual hard disks that were attached to the old VM configuration.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] The assistant provided a further updated script that copies over all network adapters and re-attaches any additional virtual hard disks from the old VM configuration to the new one.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explained that the script uses the `Get-VMHardDiskDrive` cmdlet to get all virtual hard disks from the old VM configuration and re-attaches each disk to the new VM configuration, skipping the converted vhdx file.
